subject: Reserved capacity: pricing corridor, credit fallback & approval checklist
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie@brightlabs.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask: pricing corridor + credit fallback

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightLabs is progressing toward a reserved-capacity decision but procurement needs clarity on how we protect against GPU market moves. Specifically: 

- We need a pricing corridor (upper/lower) for the committed SKU prices over the first 12 months, or an explicit credit mechanism if market spot increases exceed X%.
- A clear approval path and checklist so our CFO can sign off without further legal delays.
- Any one-time credits or kickoff discounts you can provide to offset initial ramp costs.

Can you share a short proposal (term + what triggers credits) by EOD Thursday? We’d like to finalize commercial terms for the exec packet.

Attachments: procurement-brief-2026-09.pdf (we referenced workload profile and expected Q4 ramp).

Best,
Sophie Park
Head of Procurement, BrightLabs

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@brightlabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask: pricing corridor + credit fallback

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clear ask and the procurement brief. We’ve sketched a practical approach that balances Redwood’s capacity planning constraints with BrightLabs’ need for cost protection:

Proposal (high level):
- Term: 12 month reserved commit (quarterly draw schedule) with optional 1x renewal option.
- Pricing corridor: baseline price per reserved-hour with a symmetric +/- 12% corridor for the first 6 months. If the market index moves beyond +12%, we provide a credit equal to 50% of exposure above the 12% cap for the following quarter (applies up to a 25% index move).
- Floor protection: if market drops below -12%, prices are not bumped up (no retroactive credits).
- Kickoff credit: one-time onboarding credit of USD 50k applied to first invoice if E-sign by Sep 30.
- Approval checklist: internal approvals required — Sales Lead, Revenue Ops, and Finance (CFO sign-off for any >USD 100k credit).

I’m attaching a concise spreadsheet with SKU-level modeling and a draft pricing-corridor PDF. Please note the corridor triggers are tied to our GPU index (referenced in the spreadsheet).

Next step: happy to schedule a 30-min call with procurement + finance to walk through the model. If acceptable, we’ll route for internal approval this week.

Attachments: proposed_commit_term.xlsx, pricing-corridor-draft.pdf

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Reserved capacity ask: pricing corridor + credit fallback — approval checklist request

Team —

Forwarding BrightLabs’ request and Marcus’ proposed approach. Key internal questions for approvals: 

1) The 50% exposure credit above +12% is our proposed cap — Finance needs a one-page risk note that quantifies worst-case P&L exposure over 12 months.
2) Onboarding credit USD 50k: Sales supports for competitive reasons but require exec approval if we pair with larger concession elsewhere.
3) Trigger definition: We must lock to a specific GPU market index (monthly) and name the index in the contract. Legal will not accept vague language.

I’ve created an "approval-checklist.docx" with required signatories and linked controls. Sean — can you confirm if CFO review is required for the credit mechanism as described? Vanessa — can you weigh in on the operational impact for Dedicated fleet allocation if BrightLabs exercises full draw in Q1?

Kimberly Park
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Reserved capacity ask: pricing corridor + credit fallback — approval checklist request

Kimberly / Marcus —

I’ve reviewed the spreadsheet. Initial read: the 50% pass-through credit above the 12% corridor is reasonable as long as we:

- Limit total contingency exposure to USD 500k across the entire fiscal quarter for this deal (we can do this with a conditional cap clause).
- Require CFO sign-off for any payout that would exceed USD 100k in a single quarter (this aligns with our quarterly financial guardrails).

Operationally, Vanessa — if BrightLabs fully ramps in Q1, we’ll need committed-capacity reserved in Rack Group A (NVL-like SKUs) and a staging window — can you confirm if we have the headroom? If not, we’ll need to propose a phased activation (50% immediate, 50% on month 4).

If everyone is aligned, I’m prepared to provide the executive note for CFO approval today.

—Sean

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@brightlabs.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask: pricing corridor + credit fallback — final approval path and next steps

Sophie —

Thanks for the patience. Quick summary of what we’ve approved internally and what we’ll present in the commercial packet: 

- Term: 12 months, quarterly draw schedule; optional 1x renewal.
- Pricing corridor: +/- 12% baseline for months 0–6. Credit: 50% of exposure above +12% applied to the next invoice quarter, capped at USD 500k total exposure per quarter.
- Onboarding credit: USD 50k if contract is fully executed by Sep 30.
- Activation: phased activation option (50% immediate, remainder on month 4) if Dedicated pool headroom is constrained.
- Approvals: CFO sign-off required for any single-quarter credit > USD 100k. Legal will include explicit reference to the GPU market index (monthly published index) and the exact trigger language.

Next steps: 
1) Sophie, please confirm acceptance of the corridor + credit cap model by EOD Monday.
2) If yes, I’ll route the executive note (with Sean’s financial guardrails) to our CFO for sign-off.
3) We’ll then issue the commercial packet and start DocuSign (link below).
